fileNodes.name: MySQL_solutions.ipynb

fileNodes.name: MySQL.ipynb
fileNodes.summary: Introductory notebook on RDBMS concepts using MySQL, covering creating a connection to the MySQL Docker container (interactively and via mysql.connector), running basic SQL commands, and querying the IMDb dataset.

fileNodes.name: README.md

fileNodes.name: 00_single_threaded.py
fileNodes.summary: Baseline script that sums a large range of integers single-threaded and times the execution, used as a performance reference point before introducing threading.

fileNodes.name: my_sum
fileNodes.summary: Sums integers in the range [a, b) in a simple loop and prints the result.

fileNodes.name: 01_multi_threaded.py
fileNodes.summary: Demonstrates basic Python multithreading by splitting the same summation workload across two Thread instances running the shared my_sum function concurrently, with start/join semantics explained in comments.

fileNodes.name: my_sum
fileNodes.summary: Sums integers in the range [a, b) and prints the result; invoked concurrently by two threads splitting the workload in half.

fileNodes.name: 02_multi_threaded_local_data.py
fileNodes.summary: Variant of the multithreaded summation example that introduces threading.local() to illustrate (and contrast against) explicit thread-local storage, though the accumulator is still a plain local variable in practice.

fileNodes.name: my_sum
fileNodes.summary: Sums integers in the range [a, b), initializing a threading.local() instance to demonstrate thread-local memory before falling back to a plain per-call accumulator.

fileNodes.name: 03_multi_threaded_nolock.py
fileNodes.summary: Demonstrates a race condition by having two threads concurrently mutate shared global state (COMMON_COUNTER and COMMON_LIST) without synchronization, then cross-checks and highlights the resulting inconsistency in red using colorama.

fileNodes.name: my_sum_mod
fileNodes.summary: Sums integers in [a, b) while unsynchronized-mutating shared globals COMMON_COUNTER and COMMON_LIST whenever a value is a multiple of m, exposing a race condition across concurrent threads.

fileNodes.name: 03extra_minimal_race_condition.py
fileNodes.summary: Minimal reproducible race condition example spawning 10 threads that all increment a shared global counter without locking, typically producing a final value less than the expected 10,000,000 due to lost updates.

fileNodes.name: increment
fileNodes.summary: Increments a shared global counter max_val times without synchronization, used as the target function for 10 concurrent threads to expose a race condition.

fileNodes.name: 04_multi_threaded_lock.py
fileNodes.summary: Fixes the race condition from the nolock example by wrapping the shared-state mutation of COMMON_COUNTER and COMMON_LIST in a threading.Lock acquire/release pair, guaranteeing consistent results across concurrent threads.

fileNodes.name: my_sum_mod
fileNodes.summary: Sums integers in [a, b) while safely mutating shared globals COMMON_COUNTER and COMMON_LIST inside a lock-protected critical section whenever a value is a multiple of m.

fileNodes.name: 04extra_minimal_race_condition_with_lock.py
fileNodes.summary: Minimal demonstration of a race condition fix using threading.Lock, where 10 threads increment a shared global counter safely inside a critical section.

fileNodes.name: increment
fileNodes.summary: Increments a shared global counter max_val times, guarding each increment with a lock acquire/release to avoid a race condition.

fileNodes.name: 05_multi_threaded_pool_lock.py
fileNodes.summary: Demonstrates ThreadPoolExecutor with a shared Lock to safely aggregate a common counter and list while four threads each sum a partition of a large range.

fileNodes.name: my_sum_mod
fileNodes.summary: Sums integers in [a, b) and, for multiples of m, safely updates a shared counter and list under a lock; returns the partial sum.

fileNodes.name: 06_multi_threaded_pool_queue.py
fileNodes.summary: Demonstrates ThreadPoolExecutor combined with a thread-safe queue.Queue as an alternative to explicit locking for collecting values found by concurrent worker threads.

fileNodes.name: my_sum_mod
fileNodes.summary: Sums integers in [a, b) and pushes multiples of m onto a shared thread-safe queue instead of using a lock; returns the partial sum.

fileNodes.name: 07_multi_processing.py
fileNodes.summary: Basic example of true parallelism using multiprocessing.Process, spawning two separate OS processes that each sum half of a large integer range concurrently.

fileNodes.name: my_sum
fileNodes.summary: Sums integers in the range [a, b) and prints the result; used as the target function for each spawned process.

fileNodes.name: 08_multi_processing_pool_starmap.py
fileNodes.summary: Demonstrates multiprocessing.Pool.starmap to distribute a range-sum computation across 4 worker processes with a blocking call that returns all results at once.

fileNodes.name: my_sum
fileNodes.summary: Sums integers in the range [a, b), prints, and returns the result; distributed across a process pool via starmap.

fileNodes.name: 09_multi_processing_pool_starmapasync.py
fileNodes.summary: Demonstrates the non-blocking multiprocessing.Pool.starmap_async API, polling readiness in a loop while sub-processes compute partial sums in the background.

fileNodes.name: my_sum
fileNodes.summary: Sums integers in the range [a, b), prints, and returns the result; distributed asynchronously across a process pool via starmap_async.

fileNodes.name: cpu_intensive.py
fileNodes.summary: Sequential baseline for a CPU-bound Monte Carlo integration benchmark, running 10 chunks of a numerical integration one after another without any concurrency.

fileNodes.name: f
fileNodes.summary: Arbitrary mathematical function sin(1/(x*(2-x)))^2 used as the integrand for the Monte Carlo integration.

fileNodes.name: cpu_function
fileNodes.summary: Performs a seeded Monte Carlo integration of f(x) over 2 million random samples and returns the hit count and sample size.

fileNodes.name: cpu_intensive_threading.py
fileNodes.summary: Runs the same CPU-bound Monte Carlo integration as cpu_intensive.py but distributes the 10 chunks across a ThreadPoolExecutor, illustrating that threading provides no speedup for CPU-bound work due to the GIL.

fileNodes.name: f
fileNodes.summary: Arbitrary mathematical function sin(1/(x*(2-x)))^2 used as the integrand for the Monte Carlo integration.

fileNodes.name: cpu_function
fileNodes.summary: Performs a seeded Monte Carlo integration of f(x) over 2 million random samples and returns the hit count and sample size; submitted as a task to a ThreadPoolExecutor.

fileNodes.name: cpu_intensive_multiprocessing.py
fileNodes.summary: Runs the same CPU-bound Monte Carlo integration as cpu_intensive.py but distributes the 10 chunks across separate processes, demonstrating real parallel speedup for CPU-bound work by bypassing the GIL.

fileNodes.name: f
fileNodes.summary: Arbitrary mathematical function sin(1/(x*(2-x)))^2 used as the integrand for the Monte Carlo integration.

fileNodes.name: cpu_function
fileNodes.summary: Performs a seeded Monte Carlo integration of f(x) over 2 million random samples and returns the hit count and sample size; distributed across worker processes.

fileNodes.name: io_intensive.py
fileNodes.summary: Sequential baseline for an I/O-bound benchmark that downloads a list of remote image URLs one at a time and saves each to disk under a content-hashed filename.

fileNodes.name: io_function
fileNodes.summary: Fetches a remote file over HTTP, computes an MD5 hash of its content for the filename, and writes the file to the local pics directory.

fileNodes.name: io_intensive_threading.py
fileNodes.summary: Runs the same I/O-bound URL-fetching benchmark as io_intensive.py but distributes the downloads across a ThreadPoolExecutor, showing that threading speeds up I/O-bound work because the GIL is released during blocking network calls.

fileNodes.name: io_function
fileNodes.summary: Fetches a remote file over HTTP, computes an MD5 hash of its content for the filename, and writes the file to the local pics directory; submitted as a task to a ThreadPoolExecutor.

fileNodes.name: io_intensive_multiprocessing.py
fileNodes.summary: Runs the same I/O-bound URL-fetching benchmark as io_intensive.py but distributes the downloads across separate processes, used to compare process-based vs thread-based vs sequential I/O concurrency.

fileNodes.name: io_function
fileNodes.summary: Fetches a remote file over HTTP, computes an MD5 hash of its content for the filename, and writes the file to the local pics directory; distributed across worker processes.

fileNodes.summary: Explains the threading and multiprocessing lecture module, covering the Python GIL, installing multiple Python versions via deadsnakes, monitoring CPU usage with htop, and pinning processes to CPUs with taskset.

fileNodes.name: docker-compose.yml

fileNodes.name: spark-master

fileNodes.name: spark-worker
fileNodes.summary: Spark worker node that connects to spark-master and provides processing capacity, configurable via SPARK_WORKER_CORES and SPARK_WORKER_MEMORY, and scalable to multiple replicas.

fileNodes.name: jupyter-notebook
fileNodes.summary: Jupyter notebook service bundling the Spark client and Python interpreter, exposing the notebook UI on host port 1234 and the Spark application UI on port 4040.

fileNodes.name: README.md
fileNodes.summary: Guide for the PySpark module explaining the Docker-based cluster setup (master, worker(s), Jupyter client), how to start/scale/stop the cluster, and a summary of the topics covered in Lectures 1-3 (core Spark, DataFrames, structured streaming).

fileNodes.name: Lecture1.ipynb
fileNodes.summary: Introductory PySpark notebook covering connecting to a Dockerized Spark cluster, creating a Spark Session and Spark Context, basic RDD operations (parallelize, map, reduce), the Spark application Web UI, word count, computing pi via Monte Carlo, and a distributed gradient descent exercise.

fileNodes.name: Lecture1_solutions.ipynb
fileNodes.summary: Solutions companion to Lecture1.ipynb, providing completed implementations of the Spark Session setup, RDD operations, word count, pi estimation, and distributed gradient descent exercises.

fileNodes.name: Lecture2.ipynb
fileNodes.summary: PySpark DataFrames notebook covering Spark SQL, creating DataFrames from Rows, tuples, and Pandas DataFrames, basic DataFrame operations, and User Defined Functions (UDFs) and Pandas UDFs.

fileNodes.name: Lecture2_solutions.ipynb
fileNodes.summary: Solutions companion to Lecture2.ipynb, providing completed implementations of DataFrame creation, DataFrame operations, and UDF/PandasUDF exercises.

fileNodes.name: Lecture3.ipynb
fileNodes.summary: Spark Structured Streaming notebook demonstrating stream processing by reading from a TCP socket source (populated by the producer.py script) and applying distributed streaming transformations to the incoming records.

fileNodes.name: Lecture3_solutions.ipynb
fileNodes.summary: Solutions companion to Lecture3.ipynb, providing completed implementations of the TCP socket streaming source setup and distributed stream processing exercises.

fileNodes.name: producer.py
fileNodes.summary: Standalone TCP socket server that generates randomized fake transaction records (name, surname, amount, delta_t, flag) as JSON lines and streams them to a connected client, used as the data source for the Lecture 3 Structured Streaming exercises.

fileNodes.name: send_messages
fileNodes.summary: Continuously generates a random transaction-like JSON message and sends it, newline-terminated, over the given client socket every 0.2 seconds until interrupted or the socket errors out.
